Identify the main color (most frequent) and other color. Find the bounding boxes of all connected components of the main color. Change pixels of the other color to the main color if they fall within any of these bounding boxes, and to 0 otherwise.
Keep only the largest perfect rectangles (width > 1 and height > 1) contained within each connected component; remove all other cells.

The output is a 6x6 grid composed of four 3x3 blocks: the top-left block is the original input grid (A), the top-right block is A rotated 90 degrees clockwise (B), the bottom-left block is A rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise (C), and the bottom-right block is A rotated 180 degrees (D).
Identify connected components of color 3 using 4-connectivity. Change components with a size greater than 1 to color 8, while keeping components of size 1 as color 3.

Identify the color distribution (sorted counts) for each 3x3 block. If two blocks share a distribution and one differs, the output is the identical block furthest from the different one. If all three are identical, the output is the middle block.

Identify the 3x3 pattern formed by the arrangement of 3x3 blocks of color 5 in the input. The output is a 9x9 grid created by replacing each '5' in that 3x3 pattern with the 3x3 pattern itself, and each '0' with a 3x3 block of 0s (Kronecker product of the pattern with itself).
Identify all 3x3 contiguous blocks of black (0) pixels and replace them with blue (1) pixels.
Connected components of 1s that form a closed loop (surround at least one 0) are changed to 3s; all other components of 1s remain 1s.

The template row (Row 2) defines a pattern of two colors (A and B). Rows containing a short sequence of two colors (C and D) are expanded to the full width of the grid by replacing A with C and B with D.
Move the non-zero digit X at (r, c) down to (r+1, c), and fill all rows from 0 to r with the digit 4 in columns j where j % 2 == c % 2.

Fill columns starting from the seed column index (col_input) with the seed color if the column index difference is even. In the gap columns (odd difference), place color 5 alternating between row 0 and row 9.

The foreground color lines divide the grid into rectangular regions. A region is "OPEN" if any of its four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right) contain a gap (a background color pixel where a foreground color pixel should be). OPEN regions are filled with color 4, and CLOSED regions (those with complete boundaries) are filled with color 3. The foreground color remains unchanged.
Fill the interior of closed rectangular boundaries of 1s: use 2s if the interior dimensions are even and 7s if the interior dimensions are odd.
Identify a rectangular block of background color and foreground cells. For each foreground cell, fill its entire relative row and column within the block with that foreground color.

Identify a 3x3 bounding box containing a colored pattern, determine the offsets of the pixels relative to the center of that box, and replicate the pattern centered at the position of the marker (color 5).
Divide the 5x5 grid into four 2x2 quadrants separated by the middle row and column. Identify and output the unique quadrant that differs from the other three.
The rule involves identifying a hollow rectangle of a specific color and filling it or manipulating its interior based on the surrounding pattern.

The output grid size is defined by markers (color 4) at the corners. A template from the bottom of the input is scaled by the size of the input shapes (4x4) and placed in the output grid starting from a specific offset (2, 4).
Vertical reflection across the bottom edge, appending a mirrored version of the input grid below it.

The output is a 9x4 grid composed of three 3x4 blocks. Each block consists of two 3x2 grids side-by-side: the first block is SV (vertical flip + column swap) and V (vertical flip), the second is S (column swap) and O (original), and the third is SV and V.

The grid is split by a horizontal grey line (color 5). In the top half, color 1 cells fill upwards to the top edge and color 2 cells fill downwards to the dividing line. In the bottom half, color 1 cells fill downwards to the bottom edge and color 2 cells fill upwards to the dividing line.

The output grid dimensions are determined by the size of the solid block of color 5. Each row of the output grid is filled with a single color corresponding to the horizontal lines found in the input, ordered from top to bottom.

The grid is divided into three 3x3 sections by columns of color 5. Section 1 is the input; Section 2 is a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation of Section 1; Section 3 is a 180-degree rotation of Section 1.
Identify the three non-zero rows (R1, R2, R3). If R1 equals R3, the repeating unit is (R1, R2, R3); otherwise, the unit is (R3, R1, R2). Repeat this unit to fill the output grid.
Identify all distinct blocks of colors 1 and 2, and extract the block containing the highest number of red pixels (color 2).
Identify the 3x3 block containing non-zero cells. Extract this 3x3 pattern and replicate it into every 3x3 block whose position (row, col) corresponds to a non-zero cell within the extracted pattern.

The input grid is divided into horizontal and vertical bands of uniform color. The output is a grid where each cell (i, j) represents the color of the rectangle formed by the intersection of the i-th horizontal band and the j-th vertical band.

The first shape (azure, color 8) acts as a template. Subsequent shapes are completed to match the template's structure: cells that are 8 in the template but 0 in the subsequent shape are filled with blue (color 1).
Surround specific colored pixels with a 3x3 border of a corresponding color: Green (3) with Magenta (6), Red (2) with Blue (1), and Azure (8) with Yellow (4), while keeping the center pixel original.

The output grid size is (3*M)x(3*M), where M is the number of zero elements in the 3x3 input grid. The input grid is repeated N times (where N is the number of non-zero elements), placed sequentially in 3x3 blocks starting from the top-left, filling row by row of blocks.
Identify the largest solid rectangle of a single color (excluding color 0) in the input grid and output a grid of zeros with only that rectangle preserved.
Each cell in the 3x3 input grid is expanded into a 3x3 block of the same color in the 9x9 output grid (Kronecker product with a 3x3 matrix of ones).

A large hollow rectangle of the same color as the existing small shape is drawn. The boundaries of this rectangle are defined as one unit inside the minimum and maximum row and column indices of the color 5 markers.

Extract the 2x2 center square and place its colors in the four corners of the 6x6 grid in a mirrored/inverted position (bottom-right color to top-left, bottom-left to top-right, top-right to bottom-left, and top-left to bottom-right), each as a 2x2 block.
The grid is divided into rectangular regions by lines of 5s. The top-left region is filled with 1, the middle region with 2, and the bottom-right region with 3.
The input grid is split into a top 4x4 half (T) and a bottom 4x4 half (B). The output grid O is 4x4, where O(r, c) = 2 if both T(r, c) = 0 and B(r, c) = 0; otherwise, O(r, c) = 0.

Identify the rectangular boundary and the four interior corner pixels. Move the interior pixels to the exterior corners in a cross-diagonal pattern: Top-Left interior to Bottom-Right exterior, Top-Right interior to Bottom-Left exterior, Bottom-Left interior to Top-Right exterior, and Bottom-Right interior to Top-Left exterior. Clear the original interior positions.
Identify the most frequent color in the grid; keep that color and replace all other colors with 5.

For every 2x2 square of 5s, place values 1, 2, 3, and 4 at the diagonal outer corners: top-left (row-1, col-1)=1, top-right (row-1, col+1)=2, bottom-left (row+1, col-1)=3, and bottom-right (row+1, col+1)=4.
The output grid doubles the width of the input grid by extending the repeating periodic pattern of each row to fill the new dimensions.
For every non-zero cell (r, c) with value v, fill the row from column c to the right edge with an alternating sequence of v and 5.

Identify hole shapes in the large red (2) region and match them to the shapes formed by 2s in small template regions. Replace the red region's holes and surrounding cells with the non-2 colors from the corresponding template, maintaining the relative spatial arrangement.

Identify the target rectangle and a moving rectangle connected by a line of the same color. Shift the moving rectangle along the line's direction until it is adjacent to the target rectangle, then remove the connector line.

The input consists of three 4x4 blocks. Each block's pattern of 0s among 5s maps to a specific color: no 0s -> 2, center 2x2 of 0s -> 8, side 2x1 columns of 0s -> 3, and bottom center 2x2 of 0s -> 4. The output is a 3x3 grid where each row is filled with the color corresponding to the pattern in the respective input block.

The output is a 4x4 grid where a cell is 3 if the corresponding cells in the top (rows 0-3) and bottom (rows 5-8) sections are different (one is 0 and the other is non-zero), and 0 if they are both 0 or both non-zero (XOR operation).

For each colored pixel (r, c) with color v, fill the row from column c to the right edge with color v, and fill the rightmost column from row r+1 down to the row before the next colored pixel (or the bottom of the grid) with color v.

The output grid is defined by the frame. Pixels of the shape (color 8) are replaced by the color of the corresponding frame edge (Top, Bottom, Left, Right) if they lie on exactly one edge of the shape's bounding box. Corner pixels and interior pixels of the shape remain color 8.

Count the frequency of each unique number in the input grid. Sort the unique numbers by frequency in descending order. Create an output grid where each column represents a sorted number, filled with that number for as many rows as its frequency, and padded with zeros.

The output grid is symmetric about the center (9, 9). Points with equal distance from the center (dr=dc) are mapped to the four corners of a square. Points with unequal distances (dr≠dc) are mapped to the edges of a square defined by the maximum distance D, specifically at positions where the perpendicular distance from the edge is even.
The input grid is transformed into the output grid by transposing the matrix (swapping rows and columns).

Find the 3x3 block of 0s in the input grid. The output is a 3x3 grid where each element at (i, j) is the value from the input grid at the same row as the 0-block but at the mirrored column position (16 - c_j + 1), where c_j is the j-th column of the 0-block.
A connected component of 0s becomes 1s if at least one cell in the component is adjacent (up, down, left, or right) to a cell with the value 1.
The input grid is divided into a grid of cells by divider lines. The output grid is formed by taking the color of each cell and flipping the resulting grid of colors horizontally.
Shift the shape formed by '2's so that its centroid aligns with the center of the rectangle formed by the '3's, while keeping the '3's in their original positions.
Connect the point colored 2 (r1, c1) to the point colored 3 (r2, c2) using a path of color 8, moving horizontally from (r1, c1) to (r1, c2) and then vertically from (r1, c2) to (r2, c2).

Identify colors with the maximum pixel count, sort them by their leftmost appearance in the input grid, and create a grid where each column consists of one of these colors repeated for the maximum count.

The output is a 10xW grid where a '1' in each row follows a triangle wave (zig-zag) pattern starting from the bottom-left (row 9, col 0) and moving upwards, bouncing off the left and right boundaries.
The input grid is duplicated horizontally by concatenating it with itself side-by-side.
The 2x2 red square (color 2) remains fixed. Grey cells (color 5) are repositioned relative to the top-left corner of the red square, with their relative distances clamped to a range of [-1, 2].
Identify all complete rectangles formed by color 2 (red) and fill their interior cells that are color 0 (black) with color 1 (blue).
If a cell contains a non-zero value and its column index is odd, change the value to 4; otherwise, keep the original value.

Four 2x2 blocks with one missing cell are mapped to specific quadrants of a 4x4 output grid based on the position of the missing cell: bottom-right missing to top-left, bottom-left missing to top-right, top-left missing to bottom-right, and top-right missing to bottom-left.

Identify columns containing 5s and calculate the length of their contiguous segments. Replace the 5s in the longest segment with 1s and the 5s in the shortest segment with 2s; all other cells are set to 0.
Replace the largest connected component of background color 0 (using 4-connectivity) with color 3.

The row containing '2's remains unchanged. Rows above it are filled with '3's, with the length increasing by 1 for each row further from the center. Rows below it are filled with '1's, with the length decreasing by 1 for each row further from the center.

The 9x9 input grid is divided into four 4x4 quadrants. The output 4x4 grid is formed by selecting the color for each cell based on a priority hierarchy: 7 (orange) > 4 (yellow) > 8 (azure) > 6 (pink) > 0 (black).

The output grid is defined by the rectangle marked by color 4. Boundary shapes of colors on the left and right edges of the rectangle are placed on the output edges, and their corresponding outside shapes are shifted and placed inside the grid, moving toward the center.

Identify monochromatic rectangular regions. If regions are horizontal bands, any zero within a region expands vertically to fill the entire column within that region. If regions are vertical bands, any zero expands horizontally to fill the entire row within that region.
The colors of the concentric rectangular rings are reversed, such that the innermost ring of the input becomes the outermost ring of the output, and vice versa.
Extract the smallest bounding box containing all non-1 cells, then replace all 1s within that subgrid with 0s.
Replace any '0' that is immediately surrounded by '1's on both its left and right with a '2'.
Identify the object of color 8, shift it down by one row, and change its color to 2.
Each row's output is determined by the column index of the value 5: column 0 maps to 2, column 1 maps to 4, and column 2 maps to 3.
Divide the input grid into 3x3 blocks and extract the block containing the highest number of non-zero elements.
Identify the primary color diagonal and create a second diagonal of the same color shifted 4 positions to the right (modulo 10), setting all other cells to 0.
If a '2' is at position (r, c), place 3 at (r-1, c-1), 6 at (r-1, c+1), 8 at (r+1, c-1), and 7 at (r+1, c+1), ignoring out-of-bounds coordinates.
Replace the main shape's color (8) with the color of the cell at the bottom-left corner (2), then set the bottom-left cell to 0.
Replace any cell containing 0 that is part of a 2x2 or larger block of 0s with the color 2.

The input grid is divided into a 3x3 arrangement of regions. Each region's colored block is extracted and rearranged into a 9x9 output grid (separated by gray borders) according to a specific mapping: Output(0,0)←Input(2,2), Output(0,1)←Input(0,1), Output(0,2)←Input(1,0), Output(1,0)←Input(0,0), Output(1,1)←Input(1,1), Output(1,2)←Input(2,1), Output(2,0)←Input(0,0), Output(2,1)←Input(1,2), Output(2,2)←Input(2,0).
Count the number of non-zero elements (N) in the 3x3 input grid. Each non-zero element at (r, c) is expanded into an N x N block of the same color at position (N*r, N*c) in a (3N x 3N) output grid.
Identify all 3x3 blocks in the grid and output the block that contains the highest number of pixels with color 1.

Identify center pixels (colors 1 and 2). For each center pixel, check its row and column for other colors. If a color is found in a specific direction, place that color in the immediate adjacent cell to the center pixel in that direction. All other cells are set to 0.
The yellow (4) pixels are formed by the union of the interior region of the shape and specific intersecting lines (horizontal and diagonal) passing through the center of the grid.
Identify all connected components of cells with value 2 using 4-connectivity. Replace any cell with value 2 that belongs to a component of size 1 (isolated) with the value 1.
Identify all sets of four '4's that form the corners of a rectangle and fill the strictly interior area of each rectangle with the color '2'.
Replace all occurrences of the number 6 with the number 2, while keeping all occurrences of the number 7 unchanged.
Count the height of the empty (color 0) section within the grey (color 5) outline. Fill that number of cells in a 3x3 grid following a snake-like path starting from (0,0) with azure (color 8).
Identify the three distinct shapes of color 8. The two shapes with the same larger size are recolored to 1, and the shape with the unique smaller size is recolored to 2.

The input grid is divided into a top half (4x4) and a bottom half. The top half acts as a map for a 16x16 output grid composed of 4x4 blocks. For each pixel (r, c) in the top half with color X, the corresponding 4x4 block in the output is filled with a cross pattern (Row 1 and Column 2 filled with color X).

Identify connected components of color 2 (4-connectivity). For components with size ≥ 2, create a bounding box, expand it by one cell in all directions (clipped to grid boundaries), and fill the expanded area with color 3, while preserving the original color 2 pixels. Isolated color 2 pixels remain unchanged.
Connected components of color 1 are changed to color 8 if they contain a closed loop (cycle); otherwise, they remain color 1.
Extend the rectangle's border and fill in the direction of the pixel of color 8, making the pixel's position the new boundary of the rectangle.

Identify two blocks of 3s, each containing one 2. Vertical blocks extend horizontally and horizontal blocks extend vertically, based on the position of the 2 (left/right for vertical, top/bottom for horizontal). The row/column containing the 2 is filled with 2s, and adjacent rows/columns are filled with 3s, extending to the grid boundary.
Each cell with value 5 in the input becomes the center of a 3x3 block in the output: the center is 0, the orthogonal neighbors are 1, and the diagonal corners are 5.
Rectangular blocks of color 5 are transformed: corners become color 1, perimeter edges become color 4, and the interior becomes color 2.

Two points of different colors on the same column create symmetrical shapes: vertical lines from the points to turning points (T1, T2), horizontal bars of width 5 at the turning points, and short legs extending from the bars toward the opposite turning point.

Mirror the larger shape (Shape A) across the boundary of the smaller shape (Shape B). The color of the mirrored Shape A is determined by the color of the pixel in Shape B at the corresponding row/column. Additionally, for each pixel in Shape B, place a copy of Shape A's geometry at its mirrored position, colored by the corresponding partner color in Shape B.
The output grid is an expansion of the input grid where each cell is replaced by a square block of size (N x N), where N is the number of unique non-zero colors in the input grid.

The output positions of Color B are determined by the formula: Output Row = (Row of Color A's Base) - |Column of Color A - Center Column| - Offset, where Offset is 0 for trapezoids and 1 for triangles.
Replace every cell containing the value 4 with the value of its symmetric counterpart relative to the center of the 16x16 grid (grid[r][c] = grid[15-r][15-c]).

Identify the pattern colors (3 and 4) and the pattern's location. Find all 0s connected to the pattern via 4-connectivity. Fill these connected 0s with a checkerboard pattern where (row + col) being even results in color 4 and (row + col) being odd results in color 3.

If the vertical band's color is present at the intersection of the horizontal band, the horizontal band fills the gap (intersection becomes horizontal band color). Otherwise, the vertical band cuts through.
For every rectangular block of color 5, replace all pixels in its interior (all pixels not on the boundary) with color 2.

The output is a grid with M = N/2 rows and N columns. For each row i (1 to M), the first k + (i-1) cells are filled with the input color C, and the rest are 0, where k is the number of non-zero elements in the input.

The 5x7 input is divided into four 2x2 corner blocks. The 3x3 output is formed by overlapping these blocks: the output cells are the logical OR of the corresponding cells from the adjacent 2x2 blocks (TL, TR, BL, BR).

Preserve the first two rows. Starting from the third row, fill each subsequent row entirely with a single value from the first row, cycling through the first row's elements sequentially from left to right.

The concentric rings of the output are determined by a cyclic shift of the input rings: the new outer ring is the input's third ring, the new middle ring is the input's outer ring, and the new core is the input's middle ring.
Extend the column containing 8s and the row containing 2s to fill the entire grid, setting their intersection point to 4.
Identify the object with the maximum number of pixels and extract its bounding box.
Identify all contiguous non-zero segments, sort them by length in ascending order, and place them right-aligned in the bottom-most rows of the grid, one segment per row.
Identify rectangular boundaries of color 5 and fill their interiors based on the box size: 3x3 boxes are filled with color 6, 4x4 boxes with color 7, and 5x5 boxes with color 8.
Identify all rows and columns that consist entirely of 0s and replace all elements in those rows and columns with the value 2.

Identify the most frequent value (mode) in the 3x3 input grid. For every coordinate (r, c) where the mode occurs, place the original 3x3 input grid as a block in a 9x9 grid starting at position (r*3, c*3), leaving all other cells as 0.
The grid is filled using the rule grid[r][c] = (r + c) % N + 1, where N is the maximum number present in the grid (N=8 for the test input).
Identify the source pattern in the section containing non-zero and non-4 pixels, then copy and mirror this pattern across the grid's dividing lines of color 4 to fill all other sections.
Each cell in the input grid is expanded into a 2x2 block of the same value in the output grid.

Identify geometric shapes (squares/diamonds) defined by four points. Determine the maximum radius $r$ among all shapes. Create a $(2r+1) \times (2r+1)$ output grid and re-center all shapes at the center of this new grid, maintaining their original radii and colors.
Replace all instances of color 7 (orange) with color 5 (grey), while keeping all other colors unchanged.
Extract the 7x7 region in the input grid that is bounded by a border of a single color.
The output grid is created by placing the input 3x3 grid and its horizontal mirror image side-by-side, resulting in a 3x6 grid.
Replace all occurrences of the value 5 in each row with the value found in the first column (Column 0) of that same row.
Identify the repeating sequence S from the top-left pattern and fill the entire grid using a shifted version of that sequence, where the cell at (r, c) is S[(r + c + 1) mod n].

The grid is divided into a 3x3 arrangement of 2x2 blocks. If the outer blocks in a row (left and right) share a non-background value at the same relative position, that value is copied to the middle block. Similarly, if the outer blocks in a column (top and bottom) share a non-background value at the same relative position, that value is copied to the middle block.

The output is a 9x9 grid composed of 3x3 blocks. For every cell in the 3x3 input grid containing the value 2, the corresponding 3x3 block in the output grid is filled with the input grid; otherwise, the block is filled with 0s.
Extract non-zero elements sorted by column. Row 0 contains the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd elements; Row 1 contains the 6th, 5th, and 4th elements (reversed); Row 2 contains the 7th, 8th, and 9th elements.
For every cell containing the value 5 in the input grid, create a 3x3 block of 1s centered at that cell in the output grid.
The output is a 4x4 grid where a cell is 3 if the corresponding cell in either the first 4x4 block (rows 0-3) or the second 4x4 block (rows 5-8) is non-zero, and 0 otherwise.
Identify all contiguous shapes, calculate their bounding box areas, and extract the bounding box of the shape with the smallest area. In case of ties, the taller shape is selected.
For each vertical line of color 2, change the bottom-most floor(height/2) cells to color 8.

The input grid is divided into three 4x4 segments. The output is a 4x4 grid where each cell is determined by the value at that position across the three segments, following a priority order: 4 > 9 > 1 > 0.
For each column, the first non-zero value encountered propagates downwards, filling all subsequent cells in that column.

The '8' acts as a center point for a zigzag pattern of '5's. For positive row offsets (down), odd rows have one '5' and even rows have three '5's, shifting left. For negative row offsets (up), odd rows have one '5' and even rows have three '5's, shifting right.
Special color cells act as sources that project signals in four diagonal directions. When signals intersect, the cell is assigned to the source with the shortest Chebyshev distance.
Identify the bounding box of the non-zero colored block and swap the two distinct non-zero colors present within it.
Identify the colored rectangular shape that contains a hole of 0s and output its color.

Change cells of color 4 to color 6 based on column indices: Row 1 uses c mod 3 = 0. For Row 0 and Row 2, if R0[0] is 0, Row 0 uses c mod 6 = 3 and Row 2 uses c mod 6 = 0; if R0[0] is 4, Row 0 uses c mod 6 = 0 and Row 2 uses c mod 6 = 3.
Count the number of connected components of 8s (N) and create an N x N identity matrix with 8s on the diagonal.
Retain the values of the middle column and set all other columns to 0.
For every non-zero value v at position (r, c) in the input grid, place v at all positions (r+i, c+i) in the 6x6 output grid where r+i < 6 and c+i < 6.
The output is the top-left 2x2 block of the input grid, which serves as a repeating unit throughout the grid.
Identify connected components of color 5. If a component has exactly 6 elements, replace it with color 2; otherwise, replace it with color 1.
For every cell containing a 1, place 2 above, 8 below, 7 to the left, and 6 to the right, while keeping the center cell as 1.

The grid is divided into four quadrants. Each quadrant is filled with a specific color based on the seed cell at its corner, following a repeating geometric pattern $P(i, j)$ that is mirrored relative to the center of the grid.
If the total number of columns is even, 5s in odd-indexed columns are changed to 3s. If the total number of columns is odd, 5s in even-indexed columns are changed to 3s.
Connect the azure point (8) to the red point (2) using a yellow path (4) in an L-shape: first moving vertically from the azure point to the row of the red point, then horizontally to the red point.

The output pattern is determined by the color of the non-zero cells in the input grid: color 1 maps to a cross shape (Pattern B), color 2 to a downward T-shape (Pattern A), and color 3 to an upward T-shape (Pattern C).

Identify a 2x2 green square (color 3) as the anchor. For any non-zero, non-green point that shares a row or column with the square's edges, draw a line of that point's color connecting the point to the nearest edge of the square.
Swap all occurrences of the value 5 with 8 and all occurrences of 8 with 5.
The output is a 1xN grid where N is the count of non-zero cells in the input, and all cells share the color of the non-zero cells.
Fill the interior of the grey (5) boundary with azure (8) and extend a line of azure (8) from the gap in the boundary to the edge of the grid.
Identify all areas of color 0 that are completely enclosed by boundaries of color 2. Fill these enclosed "holes" with color 3 and set all other cells in the grid to 0.

The new rectangle (color 8) is placed in the gap between the two existing rectangles. Its range along the axis of separation is the gap itself, and its range along the perpendicular axis is the intersection of the two existing rectangles' ranges, excluding the first and last indices.

Identify the 2x2 block of color 8 as the target. Extract the single colored pixel from each of the four 5x5 quadrants of the grid and map their colors to the corresponding positions (TL, TR, BL, BR) within the 2x2 target block, setting all other pixels to 0.
Pixels in the inner grid move to the edge closest to the border that matches their color (Top, Bottom, Left, or Right). Pixels that do not match any border color are removed.
Identify a 3x3 ring of a single color and output the color of the center pixel.
Identify the repeating pattern starting from column 1 to the end of the initial sequence in each row, and extend that pattern across the entire width of the grid while keeping column 0 unchanged.

When a cell with value 3 is adjacent (horizontally or vertically) to a cell with value 2, the cell with value 3 transforms into 8 and the cell with value 2 transforms into 0. All other cells remain unchanged.

Split the 3x6 input into two 3x3 grids. The output is a 3x3 grid where a cell is color 6 if the corresponding cell in either the left grid (color 4) or the right grid (color 3) is non-zero; otherwise, it is 0.
Create a pyramid structure centered at the input column C with height H. The height of each column j is h = H - |j - C|. Colors alternate between 7 (even distance from C) and 8 (odd distance from C).

Identify columns containing color 2 in the last row. Fill these columns with 2s from row 0-9. If a column contains color 5, shift the 2s above the 5 to the next column. Copy the 2s to the adjacent column, but clear any 2s that share a row with any color 5 in the grid.
For every cell of color 2, create a 3x3 square of color 1 centered at that cell, preserving all existing non-zero colors (including the center cell of color 2).
Fill the cells between any two '1's that share the same row or column with '8's.
Extract a 5x5 block from rows 6-10 and columns 3-7 of the input grid, then reverse the order of elements in each row.
Identify markers in the first row and clusters of color 5. Each cluster of color 5 is replaced by the color of the marker located in the first row within the cluster's column range.
The cell with color 3 moves one step towards the cell with color 4 based on the sign of the difference in their row and column indices, while the cell with color 4 remains stationary.

Identify maroon (9) seed rectangles, surround each with a green (3) border, and connect these borders sequentially from top to bottom. For each seed rectangle, create a blue (1) column of the same width extending from the bottom of its (potentially extended) border to the bottom of the grid.
Identify the background color of the region containing the highest count of pixels of the special color.
Connect all original points (8s) that share the same row with a horizontal line of 8s and all original points that share the same column with a vertical line of 8s.

The grid is filled with 8s, except for a path of 1s that "bounces" horizontally. Starting from the bottom-left (row 9, col 0), the column index increases by 1 for each row moving upwards until it reaches the maximum width (W-1), then decreases back to 0, and repeats.
The grid is divided into horizontal or vertical bands; every cell in each band is replaced by the most frequent (dominant) color of that band.
Count the number of pixels of color 5 (N). Shift the cross's vertical line by -N columns and its horizontal line by +N rows, then remove all color 5 pixels.
